leviFromSTRING

Source: R/leviFromSTRING.R
leviFromSTRING.Rd

Build a levi-compatible network directly from the STRING protein interaction database using the STRINGdb Bioconductor package. Node coordinates are computed from the interaction graph via an igraph layout algorithm, so no manual network file download is required.

leviFromSTRING(
  genes,
  species = 9606,
  score_threshold = 400,
  network_type = c("full", "physical"),
  layout = c("fr", "kk", "lgl", "dh", "circle"),
  version = "11.5",
  input_directory = tempdir(),
  id_col = NULL
)

Arguments

genes

Character vector of gene symbols (or Entrez IDs / Ensembl IDs, matched by STRINGdb's mapping step). Genes not found in STRING are silently dropped and reported via message().

species

Integer. NCBI taxonomy ID. Common values: 9606 (human, default), 10090 (mouse), 10116 (rat), 7227 (Drosophila), 4932 (yeast), 6239 (C. elegans).

score_threshold

Integer (0-1000). Minimum STRING combined score to retain an interaction. 400 = medium confidence (default), 700 = high confidence, 900 = highest confidence.

network_type

Character. STRING network type: "full" (default, all channels) or "physical" (only physical protein-protein interactions).

layout

Character. igraph layout algorithm used to assign (x, y) coordinates to nodes. Options: "fr" Fruchterman-Reingold (default, good for most sizes), "kk" Kamada-Kawai (small networks, <=100 nodes), "lgl" Large Graph Layout (>500 nodes), "dh" Davidson-Harel, "circle".

version

Character. STRING database version. Default "11.5".

input_directory

Character. Local cache directory for STRINGdb files. Defaults to a temporary directory (re-downloaded each session). Set a persistent path (e.g. "~/.stringdb_cache") to avoid re-downloading.

id_col

Character. Column in genes to map when genes is a data.frame. Ignored when genes is a character vector.

Value

A list with three elements:

$nodes

data.frame with columns name (gene symbol), x, y - ready for networkCoordinatesInput.

$edges

data.frame with columns V1, V2 (interacting gene symbols) - ready for networkInteractionsInput.

$graph

The igraph object (invisible, for debugging or alternative layout experiments).

Pass $nodes and $edges directly to levi() with fileTypeInput = "stg".

Details

Workflow:

  1. STRINGdb maps gene symbols to STRING protein IDs.

  2. Interactions above score_threshold are retrieved.

  3. An igraph subnetwork is built and isolated nodes are retained.

  4. A 2-D layout is computed (coordinates scaled to \[0, 100\]).

  5. Gene symbols are recovered from the STRING node metadata.

Layout choice guide:

"fr"Default. Force-directed, balanced for 50-500 nodes.
"kk"Kamada-Kawai. Better aesthetics for <100 nodes.
"lgl"Large Graph Layout. Use for >500 nodes.
"dh"Davidson-Harel. Slow but high quality.
"circle"Ring layout. Use for pathway-like linear chains.

Tip - seed for reproducibility: Force-directed layouts are stochastic. Set set.seed() before calling leviFromSTRING() when exact coordinates must be reproduced.

Author

Jose Rafael Pilan (rafael.pilan@unesp.br)

Examples

# All examples below query the STRING database over the network and
# download a species-wide alias file (~20 MB), so they are not run
# during automated checks.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
genes <- c("TP53", "BRCA1", "EGFR", "MYC", "PTEN")
set.seed(42)
net <- leviFromSTRING(genes, species = 9606, score_threshold = 700)
head(net$nodes)

# Human MAPK signalling genes
mapk_genes <- c("EGFR", "KRAS", "BRAF", "MAP2K1", "MAPK1", "MAPK3",
                "RPS6KA1", "MYC", "JUN", "FOS")
set.seed(42)
net <- leviFromSTRING(mapk_genes, species = 9606, score_threshold = 400)
levi(
    expressionInput          = my_expression_df,   # your own data.frame
    networkCoordinatesInput  = net$nodes,
    networkInteractionsInput = net$edges,
    fileTypeInput            = "stg",
    geneSymbolInput          = "GeneID",
    readExpColumn            = readExpColumn("Tumor-Normal"),
    signal_mode              = "logfc"
)
} # }
